statement: The precise prime-power comparison. For a mixed genus-zero mapping class group $M$ and a finite $p$-subgroup $J\leq M$, the natural map $M\to\widehat M$ induces a bijection on conjugacy classes of finite $p$-subgroups, and \[ N_{\widehat M}(J)=\overline{N_M(J)},\qquad C_{\widehat M}(J)=\overline{C_M(J)}. \tag{A.T1} \] This is Boggi--Zalesskii Theorem A \cite{CA_BZ2025}, equivalently the full Theorem 4.3, applied to the completion map. The centralizer assertion is assertion (iii) of that theorem, not the last equality in the proof of their Theorem 5.1(iii).

statement: Solvable finite subgroups in genus zero. Let $M\leq\Gamma_{0,[n]}$ be of finite index. The map $M\to\widehat M$ induces a bijection between conjugacy classes of finite solvable subgroups. This proves the solvable comparison required in task A.1 and checks LM4\_SUCCESSOR B.30/B.39 by an independent argument.

Thus the finite equations and their source frame labels for $\varphi$ are transported exactly to those for $\rho_+$ on $L/N^*$; the projection to the $t=1,\eta=0$ factor in (MC.4) recovers the originally calculated quotient $R$. This supplies the finite marking comparison for the successive-prime factors as well as for the full cubic detector. It supplies no pentagon exclusion without the corresponding finite calculation.

statement: The canonical relative central obstruction. Let $\overline s,\overline r$ be the images of $s,r$ in the actual group $D$ of (B.M2). There is a finite, canonically marked central extension \[ 1\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow D^{\mathrm c} \xrightarrow{\pi}D\longrightarrow1, \qquad D^{\mathrm c}=B_0/[B_0,K],\quad M=K/[B_0,K]. \tag{B.M3} \] Write $S_0,R_0$ for its distinguished images of $s,r$. For every actual automorphism of $D$ of the form \[ \alpha_f(\overline s)=\overline s f_D, \qquad \alpha_f(\overline r)=f_D^{-1}\overline r, \qquad f_D\in D, \tag{B.M4} \] the following element of the finite group $M$ is well-defined, independently of the choice of a lift $\widetilde f$ of $f_D$: \[ a=(S_0\widetilde f)^2,\qquad b=(\widetilde f^{-1}R_0)^3,\qquad o(\alpha_f)=a^3b^2. \tag{B.M5} \] Let $\ell$ be the map from automorphisms of $D^{\mathrm c}$ preserving $M$ and fixing $S_0R_0$ to the automorphisms of $D$ in (B.M4). Its exact image and fibres are \[ \operatorname{im}\ell=o^{-1}(1), \qquad |\ell^{-1}(\alpha_f)|=1 \quad(\alpha_f\in o^{-1}(1)). \] On this image the unique automorphism is given by \[ f^{\mathrm c}=\widetilde f\,ab, \qquad S_0\longmapsto S_0f^{\mathrm c}, \qquad R_0\longmapsto(f^{\mathrm c})^{-1}R_0. \tag{B.M6} \] This is a finite, effectively computable necessary obstruction for a normalized gentle automorphism inducing (B.M4). In addition, every such gentle lift has $f^{\mathrm c}\in P'$, where $P$ is the image of $F_0$ in $D^{\mathrm c}$, and preserves the positive conjugacy classes of $S_0$ and $R_0$. Prescribed modular residues of the two conjugators give the exact finite tests in (B.M8) below.

statement: The all-depth ordinary-pair assertion. \label{task:ghost-c1} The asserted necessity of finite support has not been proved or refuted. Finite-support reconstruction is proved in Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-finite-support}. The exact remaining assertion is that, for every ordinary infinite-support pair, the continuous section fibre of the full pronilpotent arithmetic quotient is empty. Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-fixed-pair-compatible} now proves that this is equivalent to the existence, for every such pair, of some integral nilpotency class at which its global continuous section fibre is empty. This equivalence keeps the pair fixed and is unconditional. Any pair contradicting the asserted necessity would have infinitely ramified, non-point, noncuspidal abelian data in every coefficient-prime projection, by Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-infinite-ramification}. The known fixed-ramification pro-\(p\) constructions inspected in this audit do not supply these abelian data; the actual projection to the \(p\)-primary valuation vector proves that retaining a rational point at even one coefficient prime forces finite support. The unramified group \(H^2(G_{\mathbb Q,\{691,\infty\}},\mathbb Z_{691}(12))\) injects as a nonzero locally trivial subgroup of absolute continuous cohomology, by Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-h2-691}. Thus automatic vanishing of arbitrary higher-weight local obstruction classes is not available; no assertion identifies that subgroup with the obstruction of an ordinary pair. Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-uncountable-kernel} further proves that this difficulty already occurs in weight two at the regular coefficient prime three: the integral localization kernel contains \((\prod\mathbb Z_3)/c_0(\mathbb Z_3)\), although its fixed-ramification integral group is zero. For all odd coefficient primes the exact kernel is the derived inverse limit of absolute finite-coefficient first cohomology, with the coefficient maps retained. Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-ordinary-cup} independently proves that the continuous cup product of every ordinary completed pair is zero. Its proof chooses bounded integral local primitives, then uses finite global primitive fibres with prescribed inertia restrictions. This verifies the ordinary-cup conclusion needed from A.27; the unresolved all-depth question concerns the higher lifting obstructions. Corollary~\ref{cor:ghost-class2-lift} gives the exact Hall-coordinate section in the actual arithmetic quotient of class two. Thus class three is the first possible unrestricted global exclusion of any ordinary pair. Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-strict-localization} now proves the literal continuous localization exact sequence at every weight, and Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-class3-residue} gives the full integral third obstruction of each specified class-two section, including its derived-limit contribution. Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-local-boundary} further proves that an all-depth section automatically matches the given ordinary local point at every nonzero valuation prime away from the coefficient prime. The integral Magnus conjugacy argument proving that assertion is in Lemma~\ref{lem:ghost-magnus-conjugacy}. The places of zero valuation and the equal residue/coefficient prime retain their actual unforced local fibres. Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-h1-weight2} computes the full global weight-two first cohomology as \(\mathbb Z/24\); Corollary~\ref{cor:ghost-class2-fibre24} then proves that each ordinary pair has exactly twenty-four class-two section classes, and a unique such class in each coefficient prime at least five. The third obstruction thus has only this finite global freedom. Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-first-integral-class3} constructs an ordinary infinite-support pair for which all these integral class-two sections have a nonzero third obstruction at a specified first support prime. Its first unrestricted integral failure is exactly class three. Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-original-first-integral-class3} achieves the same first depth with the original factorial exponents of A.44, by treating the coefficient prime three and its nonzero global central freedom explicitly. This resolves one concrete first-depth problem without proving that every ordinary infinite-support pair is excluded at some depth. Lemma~\ref{lem:ghost-prefix-five} proves the exact finite-prefix comparison at coefficient five, including the integral local primitives at the earlier support primes. Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-passing-first-class3} uses it to construct a further original A.44 family whose first failure is class three even though every compact elliptic support test is satisfied and a full affine-cover abelian section exists. These are selected families. Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-dense-class3} extends the construction after every finite legal original A.44 prefix. Lemma~\ref{lem:ghost-finite-prefix-determines} proves finite determinacy of the full class-two cochain class modulo every power of each coefficient prime at least five, by performing the old-prime division by \(p-1\) integrally before reducing. Corollary~\ref{cor:ghost-open-dense-class3} consequently gives an open dense set of first-class-three exclusions in the original prefix topology, including its compact-passing subspace. The possible all-depth survivors lie in its closed complement with empty interior; emptiness or nonemptiness of that complement has not been established. The all-depth assertion for every allowed pair remains unresolved.

notes: Every fixed ordinary pair has compatible compact lifting fibres; finite support from all-depth lifting remains undecided.

statement: Finite-support reconstruction; confirms SECTIONS A.32. \label{prop:ghost-finite-support} Every pair in \(\mathcal G_{\rm ord}\) for which the valuation vector of at least one of \(A\), \(B\), or \(A/B\) is finitely supported has the form \[ (A,B)=(\kappa(t),\kappa(1-t)), \qquad t\in\mathbb Q\setminus\{0,1\}, \] for a unique \(t\), and \(t_p=t\) at every finite prime.

statement: Infinite ramification at every coefficient prime. \label{prop:ghost-infinite-ramification} For an ordinary pair with infinite support, its abelian \(\ell\)-primary Kummer component ramifies at infinitely many rational primes, for every \(\ell\). Its abelian component at no \(\ell\) is the component of a rational point or a cuspidal section. For every finite set of rational primes \(S\), the vectors \((v_q(A),v_q(B))\), \(q\notin S\), span \(\mathbb Q_\ell^2\) for every \(\ell\). In particular the abelian geometric inertia images outside any finite set containing \(\ell\) generate an open submodule of \(\mathbb Z_\ell(1)^2\).

checks: Fixed finite-ramification reduction: limitation proved
notes: An infinite-support ordinary pair has unbounded ramification support at every coefficient prime.

statement: Compact higher-weight cocycles. \label{lem:ghost-higher-z1} For every \(r\geq2\), the module \(Z^1_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,\mathbb Z_\ell(r))\) is a finite free \(\mathbb Z_\ell\)-module, and its module topology is its compact-open topology. Every such cocycle factors through \(G_{\mathbb Q,\{\ell,\infty\}}\).

statement: The integral Hall coordinate model. \label{lem:ghost-hall-model} For fixed \(r\), ordered basic commutators of weights at most \(r\) identify \(N_{r,\ell}\), as a topological space, with \(\mathbb Z_\ell^{h_r}\). Multiplication, inversion, and taking \(\mathbb Z_\ell\)-powers have coordinates given by rational polynomials. Their denominators have a fixed bound depending on \(r\). The quotient to \(N_{r-1,\ell}\) deletes the weight-\(r\) coordinates, and setting those coordinates equal to zero gives a continuous section of this quotient as a map of spaces. The coordinate functions of \(g(u)\), for the actual action of \(G\), are rational polynomials in the coordinates of \(u\), with coefficients that are continuous functions of \(g\). They too have bounded denominators at each fixed \(r\).
depends_on: Integral Hall collection and actual free nilpotent pro-ell quotients
checks: Integral nilpotent model: checked
notes: All coefficient primes, including two and three, are retained.

statement: Finite polynomial families of integral primitives. \label{lem:ghost-primitive-family} Let \(T\) be a finite free \(\mathbb Z_\ell\)-module with a continuous \(G\)-action. Fix continuous rational two-cochains \(c_1,\ldots,c_m\in C^2(G,T\otimes\mathbb Q_\ell)\). Then \[ R=\left\{u\in\mathbb Z_\ell^m: \sum_i u_i c_i\in\delta C^1(G,T)\right\} \] is a closed finite free submodule of \(\mathbb Z_\ell^m\). There is a continuous \(\mathbb Z_\ell\)-linear map \(h:R\to C^1(G,T)\) satisfying \(\delta h(u)=\sum_i u_i c_i\). Each coordinate of \(h\), relative to finitely many fixed continuous cochains, is the restriction to \(R\) of a \(\mathbb Q_\ell\)-linear form on \(\mathbb Q_\ell^m\).

notes: The finite polynomial parameters and actual integral cochains are retained.

statement: Compactness for a fixed abelian cocycle. \label{prop:ghost-compact-fibres} Every \(\mathscr S_{r,\ell}(a)\) is compact Hausdorff. More precisely, it is the continuous image of a closed subset \(X_r\subseteq\mathbb Z_\ell^{d_r}\), and its Hall coordinate functions are rational polynomials in these parameters, with continuous cochain coefficients.

statement: Exact compatibility equivalence for one fixed pair. \label{thm:ghost-fixed-pair-compatible} For any fixed power-completed Kummer pair \((A,B)\), the following two statements are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item For every integer \(r\geq1\), there exists a continuous section of \(E/\Gamma_{r+1}\Pi\to G_{\mathbb Q}\) whose abelian Kummer class is \((A,B)\). \item There exists a continuous section of \(E/\bigcap_r\Gamma_{r+1}\Pi\to G_{\mathbb Q}\) whose abelian Kummer class is \((A,B)\). \end{enumerate} The corresponding equivalence also holds with the requirement that all restrictions be geometrically conjugate to one fixed family of local point sections, or of local cuspidal sections, at every level.

statement: The weight-twelve, coefficient-691 kernel. \label{prop:ghost-h2-691} Put \(\ell=691\), \(T=\mathbb Z_{691}(12)\), and \(S=\{691,\infty\}\). Its image in \(H^2(G_{\mathbb Q},T/691^nT)\) is zero for every \(n\geq1\).

statement: The exact derived-limit kernel and a regular-prime example. \label{prop:ghost-uncountable-kernel} For every odd prime \(\ell\) and every \(r\geq2\), the kernel of the actual integral localization map is exactly \[ \ker\!\left(H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},\mathbb Z_\ell(r)) \longrightarrow\prod_v H^2_{\rm cts} (G_{\mathbb Q_v},\mathbb Z_\ell(r))\right) \simeq\varprojlim_n^{\,1}H^1 (G_{\mathbb Q},\mathbb Z/\ell^n(r)). \] At \(\ell=3,r=2\), this kernel contains a subgroup isomorphic to \[ \frac{\prod_{j\geq1}\mathbb Z_3} {c_0(\mathbb Z_3)},\qquad c_0(\mathbb Z_3)= \{(z_j):z_j\longrightarrow0\text{ in }\mathbb Z_3\}. \] In particular it is uncountable. The unramified integral group \(H^2(G_{\mathbb Q,\{3,\infty\}},\mathbb Z_3(2))\) is nevertheless zero.

In particular this proves the exactness assertion used in SECTIONS A.65.8. For \(r=3\), inflation has zero source, so \(\Psi_{\ell,3}\) is an isomorphism for every \(\ell\), as asserted abstractly in SECTIONS A.46.2.

statement: The exact coefficient-prime image. \label{lem:ghost-variable-exponent-image} Let \(d\ge2\), let \(24\mid C\), and let \(n=h!\), where \(h\ge2d^2\) and every prime divisor of \(C\) is at most \(h\). At the real place it has the image of three. Both support sequences are infinite. The proof specifies the permissible parameters and the actual recursion, including all its local component maps.

statement: A uniform rigid target. \label{task:ghost-c3} Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-elliptic-target} identifies an actual degree-\(27\) finite cover excluding the family of Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-original-first-integral-class3}: it is the elliptic curve \(y^2=x^3+9\) with twenty-seven geometric punctures, with its explicit cover map through \(y^2=x^3-243\) and \(3u^3-2v^3=1\). All three mod-three central classes are accounted for: two already fail the third obstruction at two, and every surviving full section must factor through the single pointed cover. At the constructed first support prime its ordinary point has no rational lift to that cover. This proves the full pro-three section exclusion using the actual cover map. The compactification kills boundary inertia that maps nontrivially to \(U\); the proof therefore retains the open curve and does not claim exclusion from its compact elliptic quotient alone. Propositions~\ref{prop:ghost-elliptic-selmer}--\ref{prop:ghost-elliptic-support-test} compute the exact three-isogeny Selmer groups and the absolute continuous cohomology \(H^1(G_{\mathbb Q},T_3E')=\mathbb Z_3\kappa(6,15) \oplus(\mathbb Z/3)\kappa(0,3)\). The exact translated isogeny identity then forces, for every original A.44 output admitting a full pro-three section, that \((-2,1)\) have prime-to-three order at every positive support prime \(q_j\), and that \((3,-6)\) have prime-to-three order at every negative support prime \(r_j\). Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-elliptic-passing} constructs an original A.44 family satisfying every one of these finite elliptic tests. The remaining case for this compact elliptic calculation is therefore explicitly nonempty; existence or exclusion of a full section for it remains unresolved. Lemma~\ref{lem:ghost-elliptic-two-fibre} proves that the compact comparison at two adds no restriction on the two global coefficients. Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-genjac-image} identifies the full affine-cover geometric abelianization with the Tate module of the generalized Jacobian, retains its exact map to the two original Kummer coordinates, and computes its image by the norms from the three boundary algebras. Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-boundary-hasse-norm} proves that these are degree-nine fields with normal-closure group \(H_3\rtimes C_2\), and that their norm-one tori satisfy both the Hasse norm principle and weak approximation. Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-original-genjac-survival} then constructs an original, unscaled A.44 output with an actual full profinite section of \(\pi_1(U)/\overline{[K,K]}\), where \(K=\pi_1(Y_{\overline{\mathbb Q}})\), factoring through the generalized-Jacobian quotient of \(Y\). Its proper class is zero. The remaining cover-lifting kernel is the explicitly retained \(\overline{[K,K]}\). Proposition~\ref{prop:ghost-all-passing-genjac} strengthens this survival statement to every original A.44 output satisfying the compact support-order tests: the boundary norms are surjective over \(\mathbb Q_3\), so the extra congruence used in the first construction is unnecessary. Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-passing-first-class3} and Corollary~\ref{cor:ghost-metabelian-cover-exclusion} then exclude a selected subfamily by the actual metabelian quotient of \(Y\). Its abelian cover section fibre is nonempty, but every member has empty lift fibre through \(\pi_1(Y)/\overline{[[K,K],[K,K]]}\). The exact map to the downstairs class-three quotient comes from \(\overline{[[K,K],[K,K]]}\subset\Gamma_4\Pi\). Thus the retained commutator problem is genuinely nonempty and can obstruct, while a universal exclusion or full lift for all the remaining compact-passing outputs is still unresolved. The order-32 quotient above excludes the residue-prescribed family. The complete attached A.72 argument has been checked: for every one fixed finite geometric quotient \(Q\), it constructs an ordinary infinite-support pair with a locally matching section in \[ E/(N\cap[\Pi,\Pi]) =E_Q\mathbin{\times}_{E_{Q^{\rm ab}}}E_{\rm ab}, \qquad N=\ker(\Pi\to Q), \] whose \(Q\)-component is the section of three. The equality is induced by the diagonal quotient map; its kernel is the displayed intersection, and compatibility over \(Q^{\rm ab}\) allows any pair of lifts to be adjusted by the two kernels. Therefore no single finite geometric quotient uniformly excludes all these A.72 ordinary ghosts. A finite collection of quotient tests has the same limitation, by taking its common finite quotient. A geometrically connected finite \emph{etale} cover \(Y\to U\) of degree \(d\) gives an open subgroup of the full fundamental group. Its geometric subgroup has index \(d\) in the free profinite group of rank two and therefore has rank \(d+1\), by the Schreier generators and relations, so is infinite. A.72 constructs matching sections of the specified finite-quotient fibre product; it does not construct a section of \(\pi_1(Y)\) or solve every quotient test of that infinite group. No proof has been obtained of a uniform exclusion through a full finite-cover fundamental group, a configuration-space target, or a modular target, and no proof has been obtained that every target of those specified types fails. This is the precise remaining target problem.

statement: The pointed Heisenberg cover as an open elliptic curve. \label{prop:ghost-elliptic-target} Let \(Y\to U\) be the degree-\(27\) finite etale cover defined by the class-two exponent-three geometric quotient \(H_3\) and the point-three section: its arithmetic fundamental group is the inverse image of that section in the arithmetic \(H_3\)-quotient. Its smooth compactification, pointed by the sheet above three, is \[ E':\ y^2=x^3+9. \] The open curve \(Y\) is the complement of the twenty-seven geometric points above \(0,1,\infty\). The map to \(U\) is the restriction of the explicit composite \[ E'\xrightarrow{\ \phi\ } E \xrightarrow{\ \iota^{-1}\ } C \xrightarrow{\ t=3u^3\ }\mathbb P^1, \quad E:y^2=x^3-243,\quad C:3u^3-2v^3=1, \tag{8} \] where \[ \phi(x,y)=\left(\frac{x^3+36}{x^2}, \frac{y(x^3-72)}{x^3}\right) \] and, for \(d=3u(u-1)-2v(v-1)\), \[ \iota(u,v)= \left(\frac{18(uv-1)}d, -\frac{27[3u(u+1)+2v(v+1)]}d\right). \tag{9} \] For every pair constructed in Theorem~\ref{thm:ghost-original-first-integral-class3}, its ordinary local point at \(q_0\) has no rational lift to \(Y\). There is no continuous section of the geometrically pro-three arithmetic fundamental group of \(Y\) whose pushforward to \(U\) has that abelian pair.

statement: The two exact three-isogeny Selmer calculations. \label{prop:ghost-elliptic-selmer} With the domain curve indicated by the isogeny, the Selmer groups are \[ \operatorname{Sel}^{\phi}(E'/\mathbb Q)=0, \qquad \operatorname{Sel}^{\psi}(E/\mathbb Q) =\langle6,12\rangle\simeq(\mathbb Z/3)^2 \] where the second group is a subgroup of \(\mathbb Q^\times/(\mathbb Q^\times)^3\). The image of its global continuous sections in the original completed unit coordinates contains \[ (3C^{27},-2D^{27}) \qquad(C,D\in\widehat{\mathbb Q^\times}). \tag{26} \] More precisely, at coefficient three its image consists exactly of the pairs \[ \begin{split} A&=3\left(u_0^a\frac{N_{K_0/\mathbb Q}\alpha_0} {N_{K_\infty/\mathbb Q}\alpha_\infty} \right)^3,\\ B&=-2\left(v_0^a\frac{N_{K_1/\mathbb Q}\alpha_1} {N_{K_\infty/\mathbb Q}\alpha_\infty} \right)^3, \\ &a\in\mathbb Z_3,\quad \alpha_i\in\widehat{K_i^\times}_3,\\ &u_0=\frac{253}{655},\quad v_0=-\frac{488}{655}. \end{split}\tag{27} \] All norms and powers in (27) are the continuous maps on the indicated multiplicative completions.
